FAQ.title: Q & A
FAQ.subtitle: Find answers to the most frequently asked questions by travelers about Bandung City.
FAQ.q1: What is the Tourist Information Center (TIC) of Bandung City?
FAQ.a1: The Bandung City Tourist Information Center is an official facility from the Bandung City Government (Disbudpar) that provides free, accurate, and up-to-date information for tourists about destinations, events, culinary, and accommodations.
FAQ.q2: Where is the physical office of TIC Bandung?
FAQ.a2: Currently, TIC Bandung City is located around the Alun-Alun Bandung area. You can visit directly or check the exact location via the Interactive Map feature on this website.
FAQ.q3: How to get around Bandung using public transportation?
FAQ.a3: You can use various public transportation options such as Trans Metro Bandung (TMB), Bandros (Bandung Tour on Bus), Angkot, or online ride-hailing services. Complete route and fare info can be seen in the Transport menu.
FAQ.q4: Does TIC provide tour guide services?
FAQ.a4: We do not directly provide tour guides, but we can recommend official travel agent partners and certified tour guide communities in Bandung City.
FAQ.q5: What should I do if I experience a medical or security emergency?
FAQ.a5: Immediately contact the official emergency numbers: 112 (General Emergency), 110 (Police), or 113 (Fire Dept). We have listed all important contacts in the Help Center menu.

WalkingUI.heroTitle:
Dive Into History,
One Step at a Time.
WalkingUI.heroDesc: Experience the magic of Bandung by strolling along its historic routes. Curated walking guides for your time travel.
WalkingUI.route1Desc: Stroll down the legendary street where the nickname Parijs van Java was born.
WalkingUI.stop1Desc: The initial marker of the Great Post Road construction by Daendels, which became the forerunner of Bandung's development.
WalkingUI.stop2Desc: Look at the grandeur of the building where the Asian-African Conference took place in 1955.
WalkingUI.stop3Desc: Take a leisurely walk enjoying the Dutch Art Deco building facades, stop by an old-school bakery and street painting galleries.
